Priya Menon: Quick sync  updating the rate/quotas doc set for the new rate-slab rounding (round to nearest 100 tokens) + the pricing tiers rewrite. Need: tiny curl + python snippets showing the new X-Redwood-RateTier header, a migration note for /v1/limits -> /v2/limits, and the new dashboard embed for 'Rate & Quota Heatmap'. Who can take which?
Linh Tran: I can do the migration note and the short example table showing how slab rounding changes billed tokens. Keep it 3 rows: request_tokens, slab_applied, billed_tokens.
Devon Park: I'll draft the code snippets. Should we show the header as JSON or key=value? prefer JSON for v2. Also include fallback `x-rate-legacy` for older customers.
Marco Ruiz: Dashboard moved yesterday. New permalink: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/rates/heatmap. Use panelId=rm-77 for embeds. iframe: `<iframe src=\"https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/rates/heatmap?panelId=rm-77\" width=\"100%\" height=\"420\"></iframe>`
Priya Menon: Nice. Linh, add a one-line note about customer impact: "billed tokens may change up to ±50 tokens due to rounding at the slab boundary".
Linh Tran: added that as doc note. Also flagged a corner case where small bursts <100 tokens always round up to 100.
Devon Park: snippets (draft):
```bash
# curl example (v2 header JSON)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v2/limits/check \ 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \ 
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \ 
  -H \"X-Redwood-RateTier: {\\\"customer_id\\\":\\\"acme-7\\\",\\\"tier\\\":\\\"prod\\\"}\" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd/small","tokens":78}'
```
```python
# python requests example
import os, requests
headers = {
  \"Authorization\": f\"Bearer {os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY')}\",
  \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\",
  \"X-Redwood-RateTier\": '{"customer_id":"acme-7","tier":"prod"}'
}
payload = {"model":"rwd/small","tokens":78}
resp = requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v2/limits/check", json=payload, headers=headers)
print(resp.json())  # check 'billed_tokens' and 'slab_applied' fields
```
Devon Park: fallback header example: `-H "x-rate-legacy: customer=acme-7;tier=prod"`
Marco Ruiz: I'll verify iframe renders in staging and report any CSP tweaks.
Priya Menon: Also add a short migration bullet: "If you call /v1/limits, please switch to /v2/limits by 2026-05-01; v2 returns slab_applied + billed_tokens."
Devon Park: small copynit: say "slab_applied" is the slab upper bound (e.g., 100).
Linh Tran: will include the three-row example: request 78 -> slab 100 -> billed 100; request 220 -> slab 300 -> billed 300; request 100 -> slab 100 -> billed 100.
